picks.what: Panorama of the city, painting (Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium)
picks.why: the great color panorama of Brussels inside its walls, every tower recognizable

picks.what: The Grand-Place and the town hall, lithograph (British Museum)
picks.why: the city’s signature square and town hall tower; caption trimmed

picks.what: The Théâtre Royal de la Monnaie, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color view of La Monnaie and its square; no photochrom of the Grand-Place among candidates

gaps: P0: no candidates. P5: only a blurry 1920s stereo view through a window (#28). P6: every candidate (#29–#34) is a modern photo of details of Bonnecroy’s 1665 painting, not of today’s city.
notes: P2 alternatives: #13 Rombouts panorama from Saint-Gilles (about 1655–60, shown in its frame) and #9 Merian’s 1654 profile. P4 alternatives: Palace of the Nation (#21) and Royal Palace (#23) photochroms. #19 (Shotter Boys, 1843, park) skipped in favor of the Grand-Place.
